 Live: Evanston residents vote in 2026 midterm elections
 Lauren Shein/The Daily Northwestern The Daily is providing live updates, including the perspectives of Evanston voters and election results, throughout the day. 
 The Daily Northwestern Staff 
 November 3, 2026 
 Following nationwide trends, Illinois is seeing an exodus of elected officials this year as incumbents have announced their retirements or declined to seek reelection. 
 For residents, these vacancies represent a once-in-a-generation opportunity to choose who will represent Evanston in Springfield and Washington. 
 After achieving a narrow victory in a packed 15-candidate Democratic primary in March, former Mayor Daniel Biss is running against Republican pastor John Elleson to represent Illinois’ 9th Congressional District, replacing longtime U.S. Rep. Jan Schakowsky (D-Evanston). 
 Democratic Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton is facing off against Republican Don Tracy to succeed U.S. Sen. Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), who announced his retirement last April. 
 Winnetka small business owner and Democratic organizer Patrick Hanley is running against Republican Tom Lally to replace outgoing State Sen. Laura Fine (D-Glenview), who previously mounted an unsuccessful congressional campaign. 
 The Daily is providing live updates, including the perspectives of Evanston voters and election results, throughout the day.  
 Last updated Nov. 3 at 3:20 p.m. 
 Fourth Ward resident Brian Hill hopes for strong voter turnout 
 Fourth Ward resident Brian Hill said voting is crucial to American freedom while casting his ballot at Lake Street Church on Tuesday morning. He said he has closely followed competitive races across the country and planned to support incumbent Gov. JB Pritzker this year. 
 Hill added that he hopes as many people as possible cast their ballots, regardless of political affiliation. 
 “I’m just happy to vote, happy to do my part,” he said. — Reported by Lauren Shein 
 Fourth Ward resident Letitia Mann frustrated by lack of candidate diversity 
 After voting at the Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Evanston, 4th Ward resident Letitia Mann said she was frustrated by the lack of diverse candidates in Tuesday’s midterm elections.  
 She said she felt bombarded by information about battleground U.S. Senate races in Texas, Michigan and Maine, while her focus remained primarily on local races.  
 “It would have been nice to have a more robust discussion of who’s running in this area,” she said. — Reported by Lauren Shein 
 First Ward resident Janet Gans Epner supports Biss 
 First Ward resident Janet Gans Epner voted at The Merion on Tuesday morning. Gans Epner closely followed March’s Democratic primary race to represent Illinois’ 9th Congressional District, with a particular focus on former Mayor Daniel Biss and State Sen. Laura Fine (D-Glenview). 
 “It was important to me that either Daniel or Laura would win,” Gans Epner said. 
 While Gans Epner’s neighbor and 1st Ward resident Liz Behrens said she wasn’t sure whether her vote would impact Illinois’ election results, she said “not to vote is not an option.”  
 Gans Epner echoed her sentiment. 
 “If you want to have any say in what happens in the world around you, you have to vote, and I believe in having a say in the world around me,” Gans Epner said. — Reported by Lauren Shein
